title: Small FPGA Multi-I/O Bridge
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a small FPGA board whose function is to bridge four PMOD-style connectors to USB and to SPI.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a small FPGA board that bridges four PMOD-style connectors to USB and SPI.

fixed_requirements.requirement: There are four PMOD-style headers of eight signals each, and the FPGA selected must have enough I/O to serve all four.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Use an FPGA with enough I/O for four 8-signal headers
include configuration flash, an oscillator, USB connectivity, and all required power rails
an oscillator, USB connectivity, and all required power rails
an oscillator, USB connectivity, and all required power rails

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board provides all power rails the design requires.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: an oscillator, USB connectivity, and all required power rails

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is intentionally compact — compact enough that FPGA escape and connector fanout matter.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The board should be intentionally compact enough that FPGA escape and connector fanout matter.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The FPGA family and package are chosen by the design agent as part of this work; they are not supplied by the customer and may not be treated as a given.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Choose the FPGA family and package yourself

fixed_requirements.requirement: The power-sequencing assumptions are documented as a deliverable of the design.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Choose the FPGA family and package yourself and document the power-sequencing assumptions.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated requirements are authoritative; open choices are to be made and documented as engineering decisions, not resolved by inventing hidden user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

fixed_requirements.requirement: This repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic does not accumulate in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board has an SPI interface: SPI is the second named endpoint of the bridge, so the interface itself must exist, even though its role, signal count, rate and physical interface are left open.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a small FPGA board that bridges four PMOD-style connectors to USB and SPI.

open_decisions.decision: Which FPGA family, device and package, and how many usable I/O, banks and clock-capable pins that device provides.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief explicitly hands this choice to the designer and names no vendor, family, density or package.

open_decisions.decision: How USB connectivity is implemented — inside the FPGA, via a separate interface device, or otherwise — and which USB speed class and role the board presents.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'USB connectivity' and says nothing about speed, role, or which device terminates the link.

open_decisions.decision: USB connector type, orientation and placement on the board.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no connector and gives no mechanical interface requirements.

open_decisions.decision: The SPI side of the bridge: whether the board is SPI host or peripheral, how many chip selects and signals, clock rate, and whether SPI appears on a dedicated connector, on a header, or on one of the PMOD sites.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists SPI as a bridge endpoint, which fixes that the interface exists, but fixes no role, rate, pin count or physical interface for it.

open_decisions.decision: Number of supply rails, their voltages, the input power source (bus-powered from USB versus an external input), and regulator topology for each rail — switching, linear or a mix.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'all required power rails' but the rail set follows from the FPGA choice, which is itself open; no voltage, input source or topology is stated.

open_decisions.decision: The power-sequencing mechanism — dedicated sequencer, enable chaining, ordered soft-start, or supervisor — plus any power-good monitoring and reset release scheme.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires the sequencing assumptions to be documented but prescribes no mechanism or ordering.

open_decisions.decision: Oscillator type, frequency, output standard and supply, whether more than one clock source is fitted, and how much of the clocking is done in on-chip PLL/MMCM resources.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'an oscillator' and states no frequency, accuracy, jitter budget or output type.

open_decisions.decision: Clock distribution topology: which pin the oscillator enters, whether any clock is exported to or imported from the PMOD sites or the SPI interface, and what termination and return-path treatment those nets get.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on clock distribution; it appears only as a benchmark stressor, not as a stated topology.

open_decisions.decision: Configuration flash device type, interface width and configuration mode, and whether a programming/debug interface (and what kind) is brought out.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires configuration flash but names no device, interface, size or programming path.

open_decisions.decision: PMOD site definition: connector style and pitch, total pin count per site, whether power and ground pins are provided, at what voltage and current, and the ordering of the eight signals.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says 'PMOD-style' and fixes only the eight signals per site; it does not state a pinout, connector, pitch or supply provision.

open_decisions.decision: I/O bank voltage assignment for the header signals and whether any level translation or buffering sits between the FPGA and the connectors.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no interface voltage, logic standard or translation requirement for the headers.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, actual dimensions, mounting holes, connector keepouts, where each connector sits on the outline, and any enclosure or stacking assumption.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for a compact board but gives no dimension, aspect ratio, mounting, placement or mechanical envelope.

open_decisions.decision: The layer count and the stackup built on it: whether the four layers metadata calls likely are what the chosen package escape and the rails actually need, plus layer roles, dielectric thicknesses, copper weights, and whether any impedance is controlled and to what target.
open_decisions.why_open: Only a likely layer count comes from metadata; the brief states no layer count, stackup, dielectric, impedance or controlled-impedance requirement.

open_decisions.decision: FPGA escape strategy: via type (through-hole, via-in-pad, microvia), fanout pattern, minimum trace/space class, and which fabricator's rules that strategy is checked against.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the escape problem as a stressor but prescribes no package, pitch, via technology or fab process.

open_decisions.decision: Whether the externally exposed header, USB and SPI pins get ESD, overvoltage or series protection, and of what kind.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not mention protection at all; the exposure follows from having external connectors, not from a stated requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Any user-facing extras — indicator LEDs, reset or configuration buttons, DIP/strap options, test points — and whether they exist at all.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists no indicators, controls or test features.

open_decisions.decision: Decoupling scheme and PDN impedance targets per rail, and how they are verified.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no PDN, ripple or decoupling requirement; the targets follow from the still-unchosen FPGA.

open_decisions.decision: Fabricator and assembler, and the process capability class (minimum trace/space, annular ring, fine-pitch placement) the design commits to.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no vendor, process or capability limit.

open_decisions.decision: Bring-up and test strategy: what is probed, what is programmed first, whether a test/debug connector exists, and how the four PMOD sites are exercised.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no test, validation or bring-up requirement.
